annotation_provenance: Authored by the assistant in a SINGLE session, in the SAME working session as Phase 1's direct root-cause trace of the real SOTI/Manulife postings against the unmodified parser (parser_version job_description_parser:v7). Per this project's own honesty norm (see evaluation/m10/corpus.json's provenance note), this is NOT a blind, pre-registered annotation independent of parser knowledge -- the author already knew the SOTI alternative-group fabrication and the Manulife soft-skill fabrication mechanisms before writing a single control here, and several controls (m10e-a5, m10e-d6, m10e-e5, m10e-i11) are direct restatements or generalizations of the real postings' own sentences. What IS true: `sentence_purpose`, `should_create_job_requirement`, `should_produce_diagnostic`, and `technical_concepts_may_enter_scoring` were all decided from first principles (what SHOULD a correct, conservative parser do with this sentence, given its real-world meaning) BEFORE `current_baseline_outcome` was captured by actually running the unmodified production parser against each control (scripts/evaluation_lib's own convention) -- several of the author's own initial guesses about CURRENT baseline behavior were wrong and were corrected only after this live run (see schema_notes for the specific corrections this produced, which are themselves additional, newly-identified findings, not just corpus bookkeeping).

schema_notes.sentence_purpose: QUALIFICATION | RESPONSIBILITY | LEARNING | COMPANY_CONTEXT | OTHER | AMBIGUOUS -- the author's considered judgment of what the sentence IS, independent of today's parser behavior.
schema_notes.is_candidate_qualification: Whether the sentence states something the APPLICANT must already possess (the thing GitScore's matcher would need to check), as opposed to a duty, a promise, or company narrative.
schema_notes.necessity_if_justified: REQUIRED or PREFERRED only when explicitly justified by section context or local wording (per necessity.py's own documented precedence: local text always wins over section hint); null otherwise -- never guessed.
schema_notes.should_create_job_requirement: The GOLD/ideal answer: should a correct, conservative parser produce at least one scored JobRequirement row for this. May differ from current_baseline_outcome.
schema_notes.should_produce_diagnostic: The GOLD/ideal answer: if no JobRequirement is created, should the claim still be preserved as a plain-text UnparsedClaim (so a user/recruiter can see what was seen but not scored) rather than vanishing with zero trace.
schema_notes.technical_concepts_may_enter_scoring: Whether this sentence names a SPECIFIC technology concrete enough that, IF this were a genuine qualification, GitHub evidence could meaningfully speak to it at all (independent of whether it currently does).
schema_notes.current_baseline_outcome: Captured live by calling gitscore.jobs.parsing.parser.parse_job_description_with_diagnostics() (parser_version job_description_parser:v7, unmodified) against a minimal synthetic document (section_context heading, if any, plus this control's text) -- never hand-transcribed, so it cannot silently drift from the real code.
schema_notes.known_finding_i4_i9: m10e-i9 uses an ALL-CAPS 'REQUIRED SKILLS' heading rather than the real SOTI phrasing 'Required skills:' (which has a colon and so is already correctly recognized). A THIRD variant with neither a colon nor ALL-CAPS -- bare 'Required skills' Title Case -- is NOT heading-shaped at all under `_is_titlecase_heading()`, because that function requires EVERY word to start uppercase and 'skills' (lowercase 's') fails it; discovered while drafting this corpus, not previously documented in M10C. This is a narrow, separate heading-recognition gap (title-case-plus-family-root corroboration never actually fires for any heading with a lowercase non-stopword second word), left unfixed here -- out of scope for M10E's narrative/duty-purpose focus, but worth a follow-up ticket.
schema_notes.known_finding_skip_blanket_suppression: m10e-f4 found that a recognized NON_QUALIFICATION/SKIP heading (Manulife's own real 'When you join our team:') suppresses EVERY line after it unconditionally, with no diagnostic fallback at all -- unlike UNKNOWN (which still preserves a plain-text diagnostic via necessity.py's necessity=None short-circuit), SKIP has no analogous safety net. An explicit, unambiguous applicant-side qualification ('Applicants must know Java.') appearing after a SKIP heading is lost with ZERO trace today. This is newly identified by this milestone's own corpus construction, not previously documented in M10B/M10C (which addressed UNKNOWN/heading-vocabulary, not SKIP's existing blanket-suppression policy interacting with mixed-purpose content).
schema_notes.known_finding_responsibility_concept_men: m10e-d3/d4 found that the SOTI/Manulife false positives are not limited to alternative-groups (SOTI) or non_technical.py soft-skill/leadership patterns (Manulife, m10e-d6/d7): an ordinary RESPONSSIBILITY-section duty bullet that merely NAMES a real technology in passing ('Develop backend services using Java.', 'Maintain SQL databases.') is ALSO promoted today to a scored, single-concept REQUIRED JobRequirement via the completely ordinary find_concept_mentions() path in _requirements_from_claim -- the same necessity_hint=REQUIRED default (`_SECTION_NECESSITY_HINT[RESPONSIBILITY] = Necessity.REQUIRED`) that enables m10e-d6/d7 enables this too, with no non_technical.py pattern match needed at all. This broadens the false-positive surface considerably beyond the two sentences the mission brief names, and is the single strongest argument against a narrow, pattern-based fix (Candidate A) in favor of a fix applied once, at the necessity/admission layer shared by every detector (Candidate B/C).
schema_notes.known_finding_no_section_default_is_a_du: The pre-existing Milestone 6B 'no section at all -> default REQUIRED, heuristic-gated' fallback (`current_kind is None`) is load-bearing and CORRECT for m10e-i8/i9/i10/h2 (content that is a genuine qualification, or is genuinely ambiguous, in a posting that has no other structure to go on) -- but is EXACTLY the mechanism that fabricates m10e-a1/a3/a6/e1/e6 and the real SOTI posting (narrative content that precedes the SAME document's own later, real, recognized sections). `current_kind is None` today conflates two different real-world situations the parser cannot currently tell apart at all: 'this document never has any heading' vs. 'this document has real headings, but we have not reached the first one yet.' Any fix must preserve the first and correct the second -- simply removing or narrowing the no-section default would regress i8/i9/i10/h2.
